govdocs-archive_org-meditations-on-the-p: Julius Evola’s Meditations on the Peaks gathers his writings on mountains, climbing, and the spirit. The traditionalist’s pages find transcendence in the heights. Climbers and mystics both prize it. The Alps were his temple. The book is a gem of Evola’s thought.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-achille-gagli: This 1913 reference article on Achille Gagliardi — the Jesuit master of the spiritual life. Paul Debuchy praises his interior doctrine. His counsels guided many souls. A quiet giant of asceticism. His Breve compendio guided directors for centuries. Souls still read him with profit.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-agnolo-giovan: A 1913 entry on the Gaddi — Agnolo, Giovanni, and Taddeo, Florentine painters. George Williamson honors Giotto's heirs. Their frescoes grace Santa Croce. The family's art spanned three generations. Florence's beloved workshop. Their panels glow in the Uffizi today. Giotto taught Taddeo, who taught his sons.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alberto-arnol: A 1913 entry on Alberto Arnoldi — the Florentine sculptor and architect. Thomas Poole praises his Loggia work. His lions guard the old palace. The Duomo rose under his care. Florence's stone poet. His pulpit graces the Florence baptistery. His workshop trained the next generation.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-andrea-gallan: This 1913 reference piece on Andrea Gallandi — the Venetian Oratorian who gathered the Greek Fathers — honors his toil. Patricius Schlager wrote it up. His great Bibliotheca filled many tomes. Learned men still turn its pages. His press at Venice served the Church. A patient builder of the reference shelf.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-annibale-d-an: A 1913 entry on Annibale d'Annibaldi — a Dominican churchman of note. Thomas Schwertner records his career. The entry preserves his modest fame. His order honors its learned sons. A friar in the Church's service. His tomb lies in the Roman church.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-bartholomaeus: A 1913 entry on Bartholomaeus Arnoldi of Usingen — the Augustinian theologian. Henry Ganss honors his anti-Lutheran pen. His disputations defended the old faith. The order prized its doctor. A friar in the lists. His order honors its theologian. His theses answered the Wittenbergers.
